flags: Domain: every record keeps domus, the cards' category. Rooms and furnishings plainly belong to domus-structura (room, bedroom, guest-room, kitchen, bathroom, dining-room, hall, study-room, storeroom, upper-floor, courtyard, cupboard, chest, floor, wall, wardrobe, drawer, bookshelf, clothes-hook, rug, stairs, step, banister, bedside-table, the curtain records, chimney, fireplace), and body parts to corpus (hand, face, tooth, gum-teeth, hair, fingernail, nose, bowels, urine).

Likely duplicates of records other batches are making now (an ID may clash at merge): hand and face (entry-69 has manus and the same example Manum mihi dā); wash (entry-122: lavō); wipe (entry-128: tergeō, extergō); dig (entry-181: fodiō); pick (entry-211); handkerchief (entry-318: sūdārium); hand-towel (entry-258: mantēle); make-the-bed (entry-307: lectum sternere); duvet (entry-95: strāgulum); shampoo and toilet-paper (entry-308); step-stool (entry-257: scabellum); basin (entry-260: lābrum); storeroom (entry-427: cella promptuāria; entry-248); wall-clock (entry-516: hōrologium parietārium); dry-cleaners and fuller (entry-543: fullō, fullōnica); floor and upper-floor (entry-157, entry-155); brush (entry-76); fingernail (entry-304: unguis pedis); lawn (entry-507: prātum); clothes-hook (entry-159: uncus); key (entry-425).
IDs carry a sense where another category has the homonym: light-lamp, gum-teeth, shower-bathroom, study-room, water-plants, change-clothes, clean-verb (clean is the adjective), chest (sense box).

entry-68: the card cites Traupman 123, 400 for lābellum intimum and lasanum. Page 400 has no toilet words; the toilet bowl is on pp. 125 and 395 (p. 123 has lābellum intimum under “hopper”). Copied as printed in toilet-bowl.
entry-273: the Cicero quotation is printed labrum sī in balineō nōn est (Fam. 14.20), without the macron of lābrum, basin, which the card itself marks long. Copied as printed in basin.

entry-64: the card leads with extergō, extergere (third conjugation), but Lewis & Short gives extergeō, extergēre as the classical form (Cato, Plautus, Pliny) and has the third-conjugation forms only in the Digest and the Vulgate. The card's order is kept; periods are post-classical for extergō and classical for extergeō.

entry-65: the card's heading is pēnicillus dentārius (also Morgan–Owens s.v. care: toothbrush), but its later line calls pēniculus dentārius the libellī's form (Traupman 39), and Libellus I uses it; pēniculus dentārius is recommended. The card's Mir link does not say what it supports; it is on brush-teeth.
entry-57: pillow keeps the card's lead, pulvīnus (its composed example), though the libellī use cervīcal (cervīcālia, Libellus II) and Traupman 124 gives cervīcal for pillow.
entry-424: mow recommends prātum tondēre, the card's own example (Verg. G. 1.290 via Morgan–Owens), though the card lists Traupman's prātulum resecāre first.

entry-86: cella (storeroom) had no source line on the card; the record cites an added Lewis & Short link. studiolum: Lewis & Short's only evidence for the room is an inscription (Inscr. Murat. 937, 13), so it is set late; Traupman 125 gives studiolum for the study and tablīnum for the Roman house.

Periods by judgement: collocations cited only from Traupman or Morgan–Owens are modern (dentēs pūrgāre, mēnsam mundāre, calceōs polīre, vestīmenta premere, prātulum and grāmen resecāre, in īmum tabulātum dēscendere, uncus vestiārius); old words in new senses are modern (adminiculum banister, loculus drawer, vatillum dustpan, camīnus chimney, lēvigāre and ferrum for ironing, and accendō and exstinguō for electric lights, as the card says); linteum lectī and lectōs conjungere, given without a source, are ours. Lewis & Short makes lectum sternere, ūrīnam reddere, alvum exonerāre and flōrēs adaquāre classical (Plautus; Pliny). Sense-specific periods: camīnus is modern as chimney, classical as fireplace.

Splits: curtain rod and curtain pole are one record, since the card prefers virga aulaeī for the same object (pertica aulaeī an alternative); the track is separate. Noun and verb share a record, as in burp: comb, glue, vacuum, iron. laundry carries both entry-92 and entry-421; the existing clothes record is not extended. Plural forms (aulaea, capillī, dentēs, annulī aulaeī, fulcra virgae) are in comments.

Examples placed across cards: Manum mihi dā (entry-88) is in hand; Cum autem redieritis … jānua mea clausa erit (entry-86) is in close. Ē soliō ēgressum pater linteō siccāvit is on both entry-64 and entry-264 and is carried once, in bath-towel.

Towels: the notes on bath-towel and hand-towel cite the towels ruling; gausapina and manutergium are avoid terms. No card in this batch explains the tap choice (epitonium occurs only in examples, in hand-towel and bathtub), so no note cites the taps ruling.
entry-423: the card prints lampadium ēlectricum manuāle, Morgan–Owens manuale lampadium electricum (Egger). Copied as printed in torch.
entry-421: the washing-machine evidence is second-hand (a blog citing neolatinlexicon.org; LRL as quoted by Futility Closet), as the card says.
